# The Vault

> A free, private Magic: The Gathering collection manager. Each person's collection (imported
> from Dragon Shield) is priced daily from Scryfall, with saved decks, deck coverage and
> sharing. People can connect their own AI agents to their own data.

Everything is private to its owner. Agents act for one person: either through OAuth (the person
signs in and approves the app, nothing to copy) or with a personal access token that person
created (Account → Agents & API in the app). Both can be read-only or read-write, and both can
be revoked (Account → Connected apps for OAuth).

## Connect an agent (MCP)

<!-- connect:begin generated by scripts/build_plugin.py from HARNESSES, HOST and OAUTH_READY: edit them there -->
- MCP server: `https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, stateless JSON).
- OAuth (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, Perplexity, any MCP client): add the connector URL `https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp`. The
  401 from `/api/mcp` points at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp`; the server
  metadata is at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`. PKCE S256, the `resource` parameter
  (`https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp`), a Client ID Metadata Document URL or `POST /oauth/register` as
  `client_id`, scopes `read` (default) and `write` (the person must tick it). Access tokens last
  an hour; refresh tokens rotate, and a reused one revokes the connection. OAuth tokens work on
  `/api/mcp` only, and can never manage the account.
- One-prompt setup: paste `Set up The Vault for me. Follow only this page: <the page below>` into your assistant. Each page says which
  steps the assistant does (ASSISTANT) and which only the person can (PERSON), checks the connection with `whoami`, and is read-only:
  - Claude (Claude Code, claude.ai or Claude Desktop): https://mtgvault.cards/setup/claude.md
  - ChatGPT (ChatGPT on the web or the desktop app): https://mtgvault.cards/setup/chatgpt.md
  - Codex (the Codex CLI, the Codex IDE extension or Codex cloud): https://mtgvault.cards/setup/codex.md
  - GitHub Copilot (GitHub Copilot CLI, VS Code or the GitHub Copilot desktop app): https://mtgvault.cards/setup/copilot.md
  - Perplexity (Perplexity on the web in Computer mode; Comet is not verified yet): https://mtgvault.cards/setup/perplexity.md
- First tour after connecting: the MCP prompt `vault_start` (`prompts/get`); it is read-only and uses the person's own collection and decks.
- Perplexity (custom remote connector; seen in a real run on 2026-10-09, Pro plan; Comet: not verified yet), connector URL `https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp`:
  1. In the Perplexity web app open Connectors (https://www.perplexity.ai/computer/connectors) and choose Custom connector (Remote), then Add MCP connector. It needs a plan that offers custom connectors (the check ran on Pro).
  2. Name it The Vault, leave the description optional, set the MCP server URL to https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp, leave Advanced as it is (OAuth, no client ID or client secret, Streamable HTTP, Public), tick that you understand custom connectors can introduce risks, and add it.
  3. Open the connector and press Add connector. Perplexity opens the Vault's page "Connect Perplexity (www.perplexity.ai) to your Vault?": sign in (a passkey, Google and so on; the page shows who is signed in) and press Allow.
  4. The connector then shows Connected with the Vault's tools, each with a permission: Disable, Always ask or Allow.
  5. Use it in Computer mode and name the Vault in the question (Perplexity reaches a connector's tools through list_external_tools, describe_external_tools and call_external_tool). Comet: not verified yet. The connector tile shows Perplexity's generic plug icon, because Perplexity has no icon field for custom connectors.
- Token: header `Authorization: Bearer vault_pat_...` (a personal access token from Account → Agents & API). Keep it in an
  environment variable or the client's own secret prompt, never in a command line (shell history, the chat).
- Each client has its own format, taken from its documentation (read 2026-10-07); the host is https://mtgvault.cards:
  - Claude Code (Claude Code: MCP: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)
    Add the server for all your projects, then sign in with your Vault account:

    ```bash
    claude mcp add --transport http vault --scope user https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp
    claude mcp login vault
    ```

    Without browser sign-in: create a personal access token (Account → Agents & API; read-only is enough), keep it in an environment variable named VAULT_TOKEN, and put this in the project's .mcp.json (Claude Code fills in the variable):

    ```json
    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "vault": {
          "type": "http",
          "url": "https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp",
          "headers": {
            "Authorization": "Bearer ${VAULT_TOKEN}"
          }
        }
      }
    }
    ```

    Inside a session, /mcp does the sign-in too. The plugin above asks for the token once and stores it securely.
  - Codex (CLI and IDE extension) (Codex: MCP: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli)
    Add the server, then sign in with your Vault account:

    ```bash
    codex mcp add vault --url https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp
    codex mcp login vault
    ```

    Or by hand in ~/.codex/config.toml (Codex uses TOML here, not JSON):

    ```toml
    [mcp_servers.vault]
    url = "https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp"
    ```

    Without browser sign-in: create a personal access token (Account → Agents & API; read-only is enough), keep it in an environment variable named VAULT_TOKEN, and name it in the same table:

    ```toml
    [mcp_servers.vault]
    url = "https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp"
    bearer_token_env_var = "VAULT_TOKEN"
    ```

    The CLI and the IDE extension share this configuration.
  - Cursor (Cursor: MCP: https://cursor.com/docs/context/mcp)
    In .cursor/mcp.json (this project) or ~/.cursor/mcp.json (all projects); Cursor documents OAuth for servers that need it; if it shows no sign-in, use the token block below:

    ```json
    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "vault": {
          "url": "https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

    Without browser sign-in: create a personal access token (Account → Agents & API; read-only is enough), keep it in an environment variable named VAULT_TOKEN; Cursor fills in the variable:

    ```json
    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "vault": {
          "url": "https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp",
          "headers": {
            "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:VAULT_TOKEN}"
          }
        }
      }
    }
    ```

    The root key is mcpServers.
  - VS Code (GitHub Copilot) (VS Code: MCP servers: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/mcp-servers; VS Code: MCP configuration reference: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/mcp-configuration)
    In .vscode/mcp.json (or run “MCP: Open User Configuration” for all workspaces); VS Code documents OAuth for servers that need it; if it shows no sign-in, use the token block below:

    ```json
    {
      "servers": {
        "vault": {
          "type": "http",
          "url": "https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

    Without browser sign-in: create a personal access token (Account → Agents & API); VS Code asks for it once, hides it and stores it:

    ```json
    {
      "inputs": [
        {
          "type": "promptString",
          "id": "vault-token",
          "description": "The Vault personal access token",
          "password": true
        }
      ],
      "servers": {
        "vault": {
          "type": "http",
          "url": "https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp",
          "headers": {
            "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:vault-token}"
          }
        }
      }
    }
    ```

    The root key is servers here, not mcpServers.
  - GitHub Copilot CLI (GitHub Docs: add MCP servers to Copilot CLI: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-mcp-servers)
    Add the server:

    ```bash
    copilot mcp add --transport http vault https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp
    ```

    Or by hand in ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json:

    ```json
    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "vault": {
          "type": "http",
          "url": "https://mtgvault.cards/api/mcp",
          "tools": [
            "*"
          ]
        }
      }
    }
    ```

    Without browser sign-in: create a personal access token (Account → Agents & API). In a Copilot CLI session run /mcp add, choose HTTP, enter the address above and type this into the HTTP Headers prompt (not into a command):

    ```json
    {
      "Authorization": "Bearer vault_pat_..."
    }
    ```

    The Copilot CLI documentation we read describes headers for remote servers and does not describe a browser sign-in, so this block uses the token.
<!-- connect:end -->
- Tools:
  - collection: `get_collection_summary`, `search_cards`, `get_card`, `list_sets`,
    `get_collection_stats`, `get_value_history`, `get_acquisition_timeline`
  - buckets (the places copies live in: binders, deck boxes, trade boxes): `list_buckets`, `create_bucket`,
    `rename_bucket`, `move_cards` (moves copies between buckets, splitting a stack; a big move is shown first),
    `delete_bucket` (an empty one, asks first), `reset_collection` (empties the whole inventory or one bucket: preview first, the
    person's exact yes, then the confirmation; tags, notes and history stay; undo kept 7 days while nothing else changes the collection) and `undo_collection_reset`;
    `search_cards` takes a `bucket` to list what is in one, and so do the
    analytics tools (`get_collection_summary`, `get_valuation`, ...) to total one
  - tags (the person's own labels on cards, on the card so every printing has them): `list_tags`, `tag_cards`,
    `untag_cards`, `rename_tag`, `delete_tag` (asks first); a tag you write is recorded as written by your app and shown
    so, never as the person's own; more than 25 cards at once is shown first; `search_cards` takes a `tag` and lists each
    card's `tags`
  - notes on a card or bucket (free-form `vault_metadata`, split by writer): `get_card_metadata`, `set_card_metadata`,
    `get_bucket_metadata`, `set_bucket_metadata`; you write only your own namespace (`ai.<your app>`), never the
    person's `user` one, and the answer says who wrote what and when; at most 8 KB in all per card or bucket
  - decks: `check_decklist`, `parse_decklist`, `list_decks`, `get_deck`, `get_deck_overlap`, `get_deck_ideas`,
    `get_card_alternatives`, `save_deck`,
    `update_deck`, `delete_deck` (asks first), `get_archidekt_deck`, `import_deck_from_link`,
    `refresh_deck` (shows what changed on Archidekt, replaces only with the preview's fingerprint)
  - can the saved decks all be built at the same time? `get_deck_overlap`: per deck what it holds and what it lacks
    (a lacking copy is `not_owned`, so buy it, or `held_by_other_deck`, so it can be moved), the contested cards (some copies
    owned, fewer than the decks need together) with their `move` and `buy` options, and what finishing every deck costs, each
    card counted once; `priority` (deck ids) says which deck takes contested copies first, `list` pages `decks`, `contested` or
    `purchases` (cheapest first; `format` text is a paste-ready list); prices are Scryfall's, dated
  - what a saved deck needs, and what could stand in for a card? `get_deck_ideas`: the deck's cards in role lanes (ramp, draw, removal,
    sweeper, counterspell, tutor, recursion, sacrifice outlet, other, lands), what is missing (`not_owned`, buy) and what another deck holds
    (`held_by_other_deck`, move), counted by the same allocation as `get_deck_overlap`; each lane pages on its own. `get_card_alternatives`:
    owned cards sharing a core role with a card, inside the deck's colours, legal in `format` and under the copy limit, with `move` only
    when another deck holds a copy and Scryfall's dated price for a copy to buy. The roles are the eight coarse ones, a community's opinion;
    say so. Read-only; changing a deck is `validate_deck_changes` then `update_deck`
  - any card, owned or not: `lookup_cards`
  - edit the cards owned (bought, sold, traded): `update_owned_cards` (preview; asks which printing),
    `confirm_owned_cards_update` (after the person says yes), `undo_owned_cards_update`; pictures of the
    printings owned: `show_owned_printings`
  - imports, exports and sharing: `list_imports`, `get_import`, `import_collection_csv` (preview first: it
    keeps edits made here and applies only what changed in the person's app, and lists conflicts; with
    `bucket_id` it compares with and replaces that bucket only and says what it leaves alone),
    big files: `start_collection_upload` (also takes `bucket_id`), `get_staged_upload`, `confirm_staged_upload`,
    (Dragon Shield, Moxfield or generic CSV), `list_export_formats`, `list_shared_with_me`,
    `get_shared_deck`, `list_my_shares`, `accept_share`, `stop_sharing` (asks first)
  - connection check: `whoami` (who you are, your scopes, and which data versions the Vault holds)
  - rules and cards, from the Comprehensive Rules and Oracle data: `get_card_oracle`, `get_rulings`,
    `find_rules_term`, `search_rules`, `rules_outline`, `get_rule` (with parent, children, siblings and
    references), `verify_citation`, `present_steps`; the rules are read live from Wizards (no copy kept, so only the current
    edition can be read: another `version` is refused with the current one named)
  - the expert council (the same experts the plugin installs): `council_brief` (the panel for a format and
    goal, each member's brief, the chair's procedure), `expert_brief` (one expert)
  - deck analysis, computed by the Vault: `deck_stats` (with a Commander Bracket floor from Wizards' published rules;
    pass `include_combos` to add Commander Spellbook's two-card combos), `simulate_draws`, `deck_legality`, `find_upgrades`,
    `validate_deck_changes`, `find_combos`, `shopping_list`
- MCP prompts (`prompts/list`): `vault_start` (the read-only first tour), `rules_judge`, `explain_interaction`, `upgrade_deck`, `shopping_help`, `council_review`.
- A read-only token doesn't list the write tools; all of the above are read-only.

## How to answer (rules, cards, decks)

- Never answer a rules or card question from memory: call `get_card_oracle` and `get_rulings`, then
  `search_rules` / `get_rule`, and say which rule number and rules edition (`version`) you used.
- Quote only what a tool returned, and check a quote with `verify_citation` before presenting it as an
  official rule, ruling or card text. If the sources don't settle a question, say so.
- Every result has `provenance`. Repeat it: Scryfall's and Wizards' material is theirs, never the
  Vault's; `computed` results were worked out by the Vault from the sources listed in `inputs`.
  Show the Fan Content notice (below) with rules and card text.
- Roles ("ramp", "removal") are Scryfall Tagger tags, a community's opinion. Popularity (EDHREC rank) is
  not power. Prices are dated and come from Scryfall, not from a store.
- Budgets and legality are enforced by the Vault: call `validate_deck_changes` before presenting a list of
  swaps and present it only if `valid` is true. The Vault never contacts stores or fills carts;
  `shopping_list` gives a list to paste into a store's own tool: `format` writes it for Card Kingdom's Deck Builder,
  TCGplayer Mass Entry, a Cardmarket want list, a spreadsheet (csv) or plain text; `finish`, `language`, `sets` and
  `condition` pick the cheapest printing that fits (Scryfall's price of each printing; not per condition).

## Or use the HTTP API directly

- Start at `GET /api/v1` and follow `_links`. The OpenAPI description is at `/api/openapi.json`,
  and the interactive docs are at `/api/docs`.
- Lists are pages: `{"items", "count", "total", "_links": {"next"}}`. Follow `next`; at most
  500 items per page. Never expect one huge answer.
- Send `If-None-Match` with a response's `ETag`; you get `304` while nothing changed.
  `GET /api/v1/collection` has a `version` that changes whenever the data does.
- Retries: GETs are safe to repeat. For POSTs, send `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>`, and a repeat
  returns the first answer (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of doing the work twice.
  After a 429 or 503, wait for `Retry-After`.
- Errors are `application/problem+json`: `{"title", "status", "detail"}`. A 403 with
  `insufficient_scope` means the token is read-only.
- Move a collection between apps: `POST /api/v1/imports` accepts Dragon Shield, Moxfield and
  generic CSV. `GET /api/v1/collection/exports` lists the export formats (Dragon Shield,
  Moxfield, Archidekt, generic CSV, text), each downloadable at `/api/v1/collection/export/{format}`.
- Useful endpoints:
  - `/api/v1/collection/cards?sort=-value&limit=25`
  - `/api/v1/collection/cards?q=bolt`
  - `/api/v1/collection/cards?type=Creature&sort=-value` (the dearest creatures)
  - `/api/v1/collection/cards?mana_value=4&sort=-value` (the dearest cards at mana value 4; buckets 0 to 7 and 8+)
  - `POST /api/v1/decks/coverage {"text": "1 Sol Ring\n4 Lightning Bolt"}`
  - `POST /api/v1/cards/lookup {"identifiers": [{"name": "Rhystic Study"}]}` (any card, up to 75)

## Credit

The Vault is a layer on other people's work. Say whose material you are showing:
- Card data, rulings, images, set icons and daily prices: Scryfall (https://scryfall.com). Prices originate at TCGplayer
  (USD), Cardmarket (EUR) and Cardhoarder (MTGO tickets), reached only through Scryfall, never a live shop price.
- The Comprehensive Rules, card names, mana symbols and art: Wizards of the Coast, rules read live from Wizards' rules page.
- Role tags (ramp, removal, ...): Scryfall Tagger and its community of volunteers; popularity rank: EDHREC, via Scryfall.
- Combos: Commander Spellbook and its community, on request, nothing stored.
- Decks read from a link: Archidekt and the deck's author, read only, one public deck on request; link back to the deck.
- Collections: Dragon Shield and Moxfield file formats that the person uploads; the Vault never connects to either service.
- Card images: name the artist and Scryfall, and don't crop the images.
Nothing about the person is ever sent to any of these services. Full list and licences: https://mtgvault.cards/credits.html

The Vault is unofficial Fan Content permitted under the Fan Content Policy, not approved or endorsed by Wizards, Scryfall,
Archidekt, Moxfield, Dragon Shield or Commander Spellbook. Portions of the materials used are

## Analytics (computed by the Vault)

- `GET /api/v1/collection` includes P&L: `pnl`, `pnl_pct`, `known_cost_paid`, `known_cost_market`,
  `known_cost_copies`, `unknown_cost_copies`. Only copies with a recorded price paid count.
- `GET /api/v1/collection/breakdowns`: by colour identity, main type, mana value, rarity, colour x type.
- Bucket and tag filters: the summary, `stats`, `sets`, `timeline`, `history`, `breakdowns`, `valuation` and `names` above take
  `?bucket=<id>` and `?tag=<tag>` ("what is my trade binder worth?", "my commander staples by colour"). Copies, value and cost of
  all buckets add up to the whole collection; distinct counts (cards, printings, sets) do not (a printing in two buckets counts in
  each). Your own collection only (404 on a shared one); an unknown tag gives an empty answer.
- `GET /api/v1/collection/valuation`: value, cost and gain by purchase month, peak month, last 12 months.
- `GET /api/v1/collection/names?sort=-value&limit=50`: the collection rolled up by card name (top N).
- `GET /api/v1/collection/spare`: cards you own more copies of than your saved decks need (spare), dearest first, with the spare
  printings (`/collection/spare/printings?name=` pages one card's rows). Spare means beyond your saved decks; with none saved
  nothing is spare. `GET /api/v1/collection/pnl?side=winners|losers`: profit and loss by holding, over the copies whose price paid
  and current price are both known (`summary` says how many copies that covers). Your own collection only.
- `GET /api/v1/collection/sets?q=&sort=release`: each set has its colour mix.
- `POST /api/v1/collection/refresh` (write scope): today's prices from Scryfall, 300 printings per call;
  repeat with the returned `cursor` until `remaining` is 0.
- MCP tools: `get_collection_breakdowns`, `get_valuation`, `list_card_names`, `list_spare_copies`, `get_collection_pnl`, `refresh_prices`; the analytics tools
  (`get_collection_summary`, `get_collection_stats`, `get_collection_breakdowns`, `get_valuation`, `get_value_history`,
  `get_acquisition_timeline`, `list_card_names`, `list_sets`) take `bucket` and `tag` like `search_cards`.
- [Connect an assistant, step by step](/connect.html)
- [Skills and the plugin](https://github.com/colombod-personal/the-vault/blob/main/docs/skills.md)
